title: Federal payment eligibility can be formally data-rich while fragmented identifiers weaken usable oversight
source_unit: U.S. Government Accountability Office review of federal data sources used for award and payment eligibility determinations
geography: United States federal award and payment systems

observations.period: Fiscal years 2023-2024 data testing; report published June 16, 2026; legislative status checked July 2026

denominator.unit: judgmentally selected federal eligibility data sources reviewed by GAO

available_eligibility_sources.unit: federal data sources agencies may use across the award life cycle

do_not_pay_sources.unit: data sources in or designated for inclusion in the Do Not Pay working system as of September 2025

selected_sources_with_data_quality_issue.unit: of 9 selected sources with missing, invalid, duplicate, or other data-quality issues

selected_sources_with_cross_source_incon.unit: of 9 selected sources with inconsistencies such as overlap in mutually exclusive data

sam_exclusion_awards_matched_by_uei.unit: USAspending.gov awards matched to SAM Exclusion records with a unique entity identifier

governmentwide_interoperability_authorit.value: none designated; Congress matter remained open as of July 2026

individual_payment_or_benefit_outcome.unit: no person-level eligibility decision, payment error, correction, or household outcome in the public review

observations.method: GAO reviewed laws, guidance, data dictionaries, validation practices, and fiscal-year 2023-2024 data for nine selected sources, and partially linked SAM entity, SAM Exclusion, and USAspending.gov data using unique entity identifiers. The source distinguishes a data match from proof of an improper award or payment.
observations.uncertainty: The review is a judgmental selection of nine sources, not a census of all federal eligibility systems. It does not identify affected recipients, quantify improper payments caused by the data issues, show a person-level correction, or establish whether a future interoperability mandate would improve benefit receipt or payment accuracy.
observations.subgroup: Federal agencies and entities appearing in award, spending, exclusion, or eligibility data systems; the review is system-level rather than a recipient survey.
observations.counterinterpretation: Fragmentation and data-quality issues can limit matching without implying that a specific award was improper; agency-specific systems may serve valid program purposes even when they were not designed for cross-agency eligibility determinations.

related_sources.claim: GAO report page and full-report access for federal award and payment eligibility data interoperability.

boundary: This record establishes a federal data-governance and matching-capacity problem relevant to payment integrity and AI-enabled oversight. It does not establish an individual improper payment, benefit denial, recipient harm, correction, trust change, political action, or household outcome.
